title: atlas-finserv-adaptive-qps-latency-cost-workshop-2027-11
body:
Executive summary:

This workshop doc captures the benchmarking session run with Atlas Financial (payments + reconciliation microservice) to evaluate adaptive quantization and request shaping for their real-time assistant. Goal: identify configurations that meet a 95th percentile latency SLA of <= 120 ms for short transaction-confirmation prompts (avg 60 tokens) while minimizing per-token cost at sustained QPS ranges (100 - 2,000).

Scope and constraints:
- Workload: mix of short confirmations (60 tokens), medium explanations (220 tokens), and long reconciliation traces (1,200 tokens). Synthetic traffic shaped from Atlas production traces (anonymized).
- Traffic profiles tested: steady (constant QPS), bursty (90th->100th percentile spikes), and diurnal ramp.
- Candidate model variants: llm-13b-v2 (float16), llm-70b-8bit (8-bit quant), raptor-30b-q4 (4-bit quant), raptor-30b-static-kv (quant + static kv cache).
- Hardware: NVidia A100 40GB (prod-like), H100-80GB (experimental), and RTX A5000 (edge-like).
- Measurement: p50/p95/p99 token latency (ms), end-to-end response latency (ms), tokens/sec throughput, GPU utilization, and cost estimate ($ per 1M tokens) using Redwood cost multipliers.

Test matrix (high level):
- For each model variant, run: batch sizes = [1, 2, 4], concurrency targets = [8, 32, 128], KV cache enabled/disabled, prefix-caching enabled/disabled, quantization profile = adaptive (dynamic switch to lighter quant on high QPS) vs static.
- Load sweep: QPS = [100, 250, 500, 1k, 2k] for short/medium mixes; for long requests sweep focused on 100-500 QPS.

Key findings (headline):
1) Adaptive quantization delivered the best cost-latency tradeoff for mixed workloads: auto-switching 70b->30b-q4 under high QPS maintained p95 latency ~110 ms for short prompts while cutting estimated cost by ~48% vs always-running float16 70b.
2) Prefix/KV caching reduced p95 by 20–30% on medium requests where repeated customer metadata is present; for reconciliation traces (long), batching and static KV strategies improved throughput 2x but increased tail latency during bursts.
3) Optimal batch sizing is workload-dependent: batch=1 for short prompts at low QPS to keep tail latency low; batch=2–4 beneficial above 500 QPS when using raptor-30b-q4.
4) Hardware: H100 gives the best single-request tail behavior, but for cost efficiency at scale A100 with adaptive routing to 30b quant models is preferred.

Representative numbers (short prompts, avg 60 tokens, measured on A100):
- llm-13b-v2 (fp16), batch=1, concurrency=32: p50=18 ms, p95=95 ms, p99=180 ms, tokens/sec=2,400, cost est = $850 / 1M tokens
- llm-70b-8bit (static 8-bit), batch=1, concurrency=32: p50=25 ms, p95=140 ms, p99=320 ms, tokens/sec=2,100, cost est = $1,750 / 1M tokens
- raptor-30b-q4 (4-bit), batch=2, concurrency=64: p50=22 ms, p95=105 ms, p99=210 ms, tokens/sec=3,800, cost est = $420 / 1M tokens
- adaptive routing (70b float16 for low QPS, raptor-30b-q4 for high QPS), autoscale rules: p50=20 ms, p95=110 ms, p99=205 ms, effective tokens/sec=~3,100, blended cost est = $910 / 1M tokens

Tail-latency during bursts:
- At 2k QPS with burstiness factor 4x, static 70b-8bit saw p99 > 700 ms and error spikes from queue timeouts.
- Adaptive route to raptor-30b-q4 reduced p99 to ~250 ms but increased token cost slightly vs pure raptor-30b-q4 (due to occasional 70b fallbacks for quality-critical requests).

Quality observations (human eval):
- Short prompts: 30b-q4 quality acceptable for confirmation/fact extraction tasks (0.5–1% categorical difference vs 70b in SARI-style checks).
- Medium/long prompts: 70b float16 remains noticeably better for nuance; adaptive policy must pin a percentage (10–15%) of these longer flows to high-quality variants to avoid regressions.

Operational notes and recommended Redwood config snippets (workshop actionables):
- Routing policy: "latency-first" for short confirmations (prefer raptor-30b-q4), "quality-first" for reconciliation explanations (pin to llm-70b-fp16), with dynamic threshold at 400 QPS to trigger adaptive quant switch for short routes.
- Autoscaling: min_replicas=2, target_concurrency=64 for raptor-30b-q4; target_concurrency=16 for 70b float16.
- Caching: enable prefix_caching for user-session metadata keys; TTL=600s recommended for reconciliation windows.
- Fallbacks: configure model fallback chains and emergency throttles to divert to a lightweight deterministic template on sustained p99 > 400 ms.

Cost model summary (monthly projection for 50M short prompts):
- Always-run 70b-fp16: ~$87k/month (high cost, best quality)
- Always-run raptor-30b-q4: ~$21k/month (lowest cost, some quality tradeoffs)
- Adaptive mix (70b for 12% critical traffic + autoscale raptor-30b-q4): ~$39k/month (recommended for Atlas given SLA/quality targets)

Risks and open questions:
- Quantization regressions for rare financial phrasing: need a targeted eval set from Atlas to validate edge cases.
- Burst behavior with stateful KV cache eviction — we observed cache thrashing under microbursts; recommend cache sizing experiments in staging.
- Validation of cost model across regions (APAC pricing differs by ~12%).

Next steps (workshop action items):
1) Solutions eng: push benchmark harness improvements and add Atlas-specific eval prompts (owner: Priya).
2) Eng infra: provision a Dedicated small-pool A100 cluster and enable prefix cache telemetry (owner: Jonas).
3) Product: prepare a short whitepaper for Atlas customers summarizing adaptive routing + pricing tradeoffs (owner: Celia).
4) Run a 2-week staged POC with Atlas production-like traffic and collect p99 telemetry and quality evals (target start: 2027-12-05).

Appendix (short):
- Raw experiment IDs: bench-atlas-2027-11-{001..028} (uploaded to S3, see linked GitHub PR for harness).
- Quick links: CONFLUENCE-AtlasFinserv-POC-2027 (design), JIRA-ATLAS-4123 (POC tickets), PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/276 (harness and scripts).

Notes to reviewers: this is a working record from the on-site workshop. Several numeric estimates use Redwood internal cost multipliers (confidential). Please flag any additional Atlas-specific scenarios we should include before the staged POC.
